reading.title: How Zap reads you
reading.lede: After each match, Zap adds up a few counters of your way of playing: how often you call truco, run, accept, bluff, and how long you take to decide. This is the reading they give.
reading.use: These numbers are only for you to see. The AI does not use any of them to choose its moves.
reading.failed: The reading could not be loaded.
reading.rule: Each number shows only once there are enough plays for it: at least 10 observations of yours, and the range it is in, with an 80% chance, narrower than 30 points. The reference is the starting point, before your plays: the value at the same tables as you (1 against 1 or 2 against 2, paulista or mineiro), in the share you play at each. It comes from the people who play Zap once there are enough of them for that number; before that, from Zap's matches against itself. Each number says where its reference comes from.
reading.hidden: Too early to say. Observations so far: {n}.
reading.reference.selfplay: Reference: {value}, from Zap's matches against itself.
reading.reference.people: Reference: {value}, from the people who play Zap.
reading.off: You switched on "Don't adapt to me", so Zap keeps no counters of your way of playing and there is no reading. If you switch it off, the next matches count again.
reading.n.raise.help: Hands in which you called truco or raised the bet without answering a call.
reading.n.run.help: Of the bets you answered, the times you ran.
reading.n.accept.help: Of the bets you answered, the times you accepted.
reading.n.reraise.help: Of the bets you answered, the times you raised back.
reading.n.shown.help: Average strength of the cards you showed in hands where you called truco, from 0, the weakest, to 100, the strongest.
reading.n.cover.help: Of the cards you could play face down, the ones you did.
reading.n.bluff.help: Of the times you could call truco with a weak hand, the times you called.
reading.n.signalTruth.help: Of the signals you made to your partner, the ones that told the truth.
reading.time.help: Typical time, the median, of your decisions with more than one option.
